title: prd_context
description: QA-first product intent extracted from a backend PRD. Test-design oriented: requirements (business + product), GIVEN/WHEN/THEN acceptance criteria with a verifiable flag, boundary values/conditions, undecided open_decisions with contingent approach_branches, comment_resolutions from the PRD's review thread, and a needs_clarification Definition-of-Ready gate. Feeds sdet-plan-generator (priority, risk weighting, boundary/negative scenarios, out-of-scope suppression, and which criteria are actually assertable).

id.description: Stable PRD identifier, e.g. PRD-SEE-ALL-FORCED-DISPLAY. Slugged from the title if the PRD states none.

priority.description: PRD-stated priority (P0/P1/P2 or the PRD's own label). null when the PRD states none — do not infer a document-level priority.

readiness.description: PRD maturity, e.g. draft, in_review, approved. Verbatim from the PRD header/metadata.

owner.description: Product owner / DRI stated in the PRD body. Comment authors are NOT the owner. null when unstated.

team.description: Owning squad(s) named in the PRD. Empty when unstated (involved_teams still records participants).

pdg.description: Product Delivery Group(s), if resolvable from team mapping. Empty when unknown.

milestones.description: Delivery milestones/dates stated in the PRD. Empty when unstated.

source_document.description: Path or URL of the PRD the context was extracted from (alias of source_ref).

extracted_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of the extraction run.

extractor_version.description: Version of the prd-extractor skill that produced this file.

summary.description: One-paragraph plain-language statement of the feature intent.

in_scope.description: Explicit in-scope items from the PRD Scope section.

out_of_scope.description: Explicit exclusions — as important as in-scope; the SDET plan uses this to SUPPRESS scenario generation. Record even when it conflicts with a later section (flag that conflict in needs_clarification / open_decisions).

user_flow.description: The end-to-end request/render flow plus its failure states — the skeleton the SDET plan turns into happy-path and negative scenarios.

actor.description: The system/persona performing the step, e.g. user, Gateway, MLS, Frontend.

action.description: What happens at this step. Prefix branch-specific behaviour with the branch, e.g. '[Option B path] ...'.

failure_states.description: Named failure/edge outcomes on this flow — each is a negative-scenario seed.

outcome.description: Expected observable result, e.g. 'Do not show', 'use old logic'.

personas.description: Actors referenced by the feature, e.g. ['user'].

persona_prerequisites.description: Preconditions a persona must satisfy to hit the flow (eligibility, state). Empty when unstated.

applicable_countries.description: Country/region gating, e.g. ['ID','SG']. Empty when the PRD states no country scope.

applicable_service_types.description: Service verticals the feature applies to, e.g. ['Food'].

rollout_plan.description: Rollout / experiment ramp if the PRD states one (segment, %, phases). null when unstated even if A/B is 'in scope'.

involved_teams.description: Every team the flow touches and its role. Under an undecided approach, record each team's role per branch, e.g. '[Option A] ... [Option B] ...'.

user_stories.description: User stories. Every acceptance_criterion must trace to exactly one story via story_ref.

id.description: Story id from the PRD, else assigned US-001, US-002 ...

description.description: The story, ideally 'As a <persona> I want <goal> so that <benefit>.'

requirements.description: Each requirement pairs the business intent with the concrete product behaviour to be tested. Under an undecided approach, prefix branch-only requirements with '[Option X only]' in the text and list them in approach_branches.branches[].requirement_refs.

business_requirement.description: The 'why' — business outcome the requirement drives.

acceptance_criteria.description: Testable criteria as GIVEN/WHEN/THEN. verifiable=false marks a criterion that CANNOT be asserted as written (ambiguous oracle, conflicting default, contingent on an unresolved open_decision) — the SDET plan must not build a passing assertion from it until it is resolved.

condition.description: GIVEN <state> WHEN <action> THEN <observable result>. Copy the PRD's operators verbatim (>=, >, <=).

verifiable.description: true = a deterministic assertion can be written now. false = blocked; explain the blocker in needs_clarification and, if branch-gated, in approach_branches.

boundary_values.description: Named boundary/default values for equivalence-partition and boundary-value analysis. Copy verbatim; never derive.

value.description: The threshold/default exactly as stated, e.g. 'dish_list > 9', false, 2.

boundary_conditions.description: Edge cases with their expected default behaviour — direct negative/boundary scenario seeds. Include cases the PRD marks 'example only, not for treatment' with that note in proposed_default so the SDET plan does not assert them as treatments.

proposed_default.description: Expected outcome, e.g. 'Do not show', 'clamp to 2', 'example for understanding, not for treatment'.

error_codes.description: Named business/user-facing error outcomes stated in the PRD. Technical HTTP/error codes belong to the RFC extractor. Empty is intentional when the PRD names none.

feature_flags.description: Every flag/field name the PRD mentions for this feature — INCLUDING competing candidate names for the same flag (record all; the naming decision is an open_decision). Each is a flag_on/flag_off scenario pair.

non_functional_requirements.description: Latency/throughput/uptime/security/localisation targets. Copy numbers verbatim; qualitative language ('fast') is not an NFR — flag it in needs_clarification.

open_decisions.description: Unresolved decisions with a testing impact. blocking=true means the test oracle is undefined until it is resolved.

approach_branches.description: Present only when a blocking open_decision forks the design into mutually exclusive options (e.g. Option A vs Option B). While status=undecided, keep BOTH branches' requirement/AC refs so the SDET plan can hold parallel contingent paths. When the PRD locks one branch, set status=resolved, chosen_branch, and drop the other branch's refs.

chosen_branch.description: branches[].id once locked; null while undecided.

rule.description: How downstream should treat the branches (emit parallel paths while undecided; collapse to chosen_branch once locked).

shared_requirement_refs.description: requirements[].id that hold under EITHER branch.

comment_resolutions.description: Decisions/clarifications mined from the PRD's review comment thread. status tells the SDET plan how much to trust each: 'resolves' = authoritative; 'clarifies' = context, does not lock a decision; 'unanswered' = open, do not act on. Always keep the quote and what it affects.

quote.description: Short verbatim quote from the thread (attribute the source; keep it brief).

affects.description: Refs to fields/requirements/ACs/open_decisions this comment bears on.

risk_areas.description: Flows flagged high-value/high-risk. Infer severity from language: money, compliance, irreversible, 'must not', 'guaranteed' → high.

severity.description: e.g. low, medium, high, critical. null when the PRD gives no signal.

needs_clarification.description: Definition-of-Ready gate. Every gap, ambiguity, conflict, and non-verifiable criterion the extractor hit. blocking=true entries must be resolved before the SDET plan can build a deterministic oracle for the affected area. NEVER guess a value to avoid listing it here.

field.description: The field/section/AC that is unclear, e.g. 'boundary_values[min_dish_count default]'.

reason.description: Why it is not ready. 'conflicting'/'contradictory' = the PRD states two incompatible values; 'non_verifiable' = no deterministic oracle.

detail.description: What is missing/conflicting and the testing impact. Reference the conflicting sections.

source_ref.description: Path or URL of the source PRD.
